To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
teachers can be active partners in the design of technology-based educational innovations, and that the nature of their participation evolves through time.

(1) a long-term participatory design collaboration can be successful, (2) the teachers’ role changes significantly over time, and (3) there are five distinct phases that can be identified in the development of the collaboration.
Participation in design is a long-term, complex, developmental process that is not easily characterized in terms of roles, and that is not easily understood by outsiders to the process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new kind of learning space, a space that is network-based, collaborative, and open to the participation of a wide variety of actors.
the design of network-based learning support, but the focus is on the process of design and the role of teachers in this process.
understanding how teachers can be supported to design network-based tools for collaborative learning, and how these tools can support teachers and students in the design of learning activities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the teachers' role in this project has changed significantly from the early stages of the project to the later stages, and that this evolution is a function of the teachers' increased knowledge and expertise in the use of technology for educational purposes.
participatory design can be an effective approach for developing network-based support for learning.
participatory design is a viable approach for the development of educational software.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is a case study of participatory design that has lasted five years, and is still going.
the project was a success, in the sense of having produced a system that has had a positive impact on teaching and learning.

we have developed a networked environment for teachers and students to collaborate on the creation and use of learning resources, and that we have developed and tested a framework to support the use of these resources in collaborative learning activities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
participatory design is an effective way to develop network-based learning environments that can be used in real classrooms.
the teachers were able to make a significant difference in the design of the system, but that this was not the case from the start.
participatory design, when done over the long term, is a powerful way to develop new educational technologies.
